title: The Past and Future of AI Scientists
hook: Ross King's survey of machines that do science: the components are all automatable now, and have been since Adam and Eve. The unsolved problem is integration.
key_points: An AI Scientist originates hypotheses, deduces consequences, runs experiments, interprets results, revises beliefs.
Adam was the first machine to make novel scientific discoveries via hypothesis-and-experiment cycles.
Eve established the architecture of the modern self-driving laboratory.
King's thesis: automating individual components of science is solved — integrating them is not.
Integration means joining neural learning with logic, probability, causal reasoning, simulation, and lab robotics.
The Nobel Turing Challenge sets the goal of AI capable of Nobel-quality science.
content_html: An "AI Scientist," in Ross King's definition, is a machine that does the whole loop: originate hypotheses, deduce their consequences, design and execute experiments, interpret the results, and revise its beliefs. Not a tool used by scientists — an integrated scientific agent, wired into the literature, formal knowledge, mathematical models, simulations, data-analysis systems, and physical laboratories. This survey traces where that idea came from and where it's going.
extra_html:
From Adam and Eve to foundation models

King's own robot scientist Adam was the first machine to make novel scientific discoveries through cycles of hypothesis formation and physical experimentation. Eve followed, establishing the architecture of what we now call the self-driving laboratory. Two decades on, foundation models, autonomous agents, and lab robotics make far more general systems possible.

The integration problem

The survey's core claim is a reframing. The question is no longer whether individual components of science can be automated — they can. The problem is putting them together: neural learning alongside logic, probability, mathematics, causal reasoning, simulation, experimental design, robotics, and formal scientific records, in one system that closes the loop.

King argues the payoff isn't just faster and cheaper science, but different science: systems too complicated for unaided humans, and thousands of AI scientists working together on a single problem. The Nobel Turing Challenge — building AI capable of Nobel-quality discovery — is the benchmark he points the field toward.

related.title: When Remembering More Slows the Search Down
related.hook: Generate molecules, score them, keep the best, retrain, repeat. A convergence theory for this drug-discovery workhorse finds that training on more of the past can actually hurt.

related.title: How Far Are LLM Research Ideas From Human Ones? A Reverse-Engineering Study
related.hook: Judging LLM research ideas one at a time (novel? feasible? liked?) hides a bigger question: does the whole distribution of ideas an LLM can produce look like what human researchers actually do?

related.title: Spark-to-Paper: Research Paper Generation as Composable Skills
related.hook: Not a new agent platform — thirteen skills bolted into an existing coding assistant, with integrity checks deciding which claims survive contact with the experiments.

related.title: AlphaFold: Protein Structure Prediction
related.hook: Predicting a protein's 3D shape from its sequence stumped biology for ~50 years. AlphaFold cracked it at near-experimental accuracy — and then released the structures to everyone.

flashcards.prompt: According to King, what is the central unsolved problem for AI Scientists?
flashcards.back_html: Integration. Individual components of science can already be automated; the hard part is combining neural learning with logic, probability, mathematics, causal reasoning, simulation, experimental design, robotics, and formal records.

choices.text: It was the first machine to make novel scientific discoveries through cycles of hypothesis formation and physical experimentation
It was the first robot to operate a chemistry lab without human supervision
It was the first language model trained on scientific literature

flashcards.explanation_html: King credits Adam as the first machine to originate hypotheses and test them physically, producing novel discoveries; Eve then established the architecture of the modern self-driving lab.

flashcards.prompt: What capability does the survey argue AI Scientists could unlock beyond speed?

choices.text: Investigating systems too complicated for unaided human science, with thousands of agents on one problem
Eliminating the need for physical laboratories entirely
Guaranteeing that published results are correct

flashcards.explanation_html: Beyond making science faster and cheaper, King argues AI Scientists could tackle systems too complex for unaided humans and let thousands of AI scientists collaborate on a single problem.
